newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 23.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on June 23. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The chairman of the Indonesian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (KADIN), Aburizal Bakrie, has said businesses were hoping the government's upcoming economic reforms would slash red tape and ease licensing procedures.

Interpol has arrested an Indonesian man suspected of embezzling 8.4 billion rupiah from the cigarette maker Gudang Garam. Rudy Widayanto, who has been on the run for four months, was arrested in Sydney, Australia.

The Election Committee will issue on Monday the final results of the May 29 general elections, which have to be endorsed by the three contesting parties. According to provisional results, the ruling Golkar party has swept 74 percent of the votes, the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) 23 percent and the fragmented Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) only three percent.

PT Timor Putra Nasional, which produces the controversial Timor sedan, will be granted $500 million by 13 top banks to finance its "national" car project. The company is controlled by President Suharto's youngest son Hutomo Mandala Putra.
